name: ktransformers-cpu-gpu-hybrid
repo_anchor: outline.yaml item ktransformers-cpu-gpu-hybrid (ecosystem-strategy, 2026-09-07 run): "for 27B+/MoE on this host TP=2 is not the only topology. KTransformers (ACM 2026 paper; SGLang integration Oct 2025) shows 3-28x MoE speedups via CPU-resident experts + GPU attention/shared-experts, 220+ tok/s aggregate on trillion-param MoE with one consumer GPU. Feasibility on 2x Turing + host CPU RAM, measured precedents on workstation hardware, and the integration surface versus vLLM TP=2." Anchored secondarily in plan/0005 stage 13 via the both-card-tp-nvlink-serving item ("Alternative topology: KTransformers CPU+GPU hybrid") and MEMORY.md 2026-09-07 (operator-ratified): KTransformers judged the fallback for the 35B MoE secondary, not the dense-GDN 27B primary (Turing absent from its README/leaderboard, MoE-shaped), with operator focus Qwen3.8 + Qwen3.8-Next. Host facts from MEMORY.md 2026-08-27 rigs entry: two Quadro RTX 6000 (TU102, sm_75, 24 GB each), NVLink bridge; verified on-host this run: Xeon W-2140B (Skylake-W, 8C/16T, AVX-512 F/BW/DQ/VL only - no VNNI, no AVX512-BF16/VBMI, no AMX), 125 GiB DDR4.
current_status: As of 2026-09-07 KTransformers (kvcache-ai, Tsinghua MadSys) is a mature CPU-GPU hybrid MoE inference stack. Paper: "KTransformers: Unleashing the Full Potential of CPU/GPU Hybrid Inference for MoE Models", SOSP 2025 (Oct 2025), DOI 10.1145/3731569.3764843 - claims 4.62-19.74x prefill and 1.25-4.09x decode speedups over existing systems, plus up to 1.45x from Expert Deferral (an approximation costing <0.5% accuracy). Note: the outline's "3-28x" figure does not appear in the SOSP paper or the SGLang blog; it reads as a supplementation paraphrase [uncertain]. The "220+ tok/s aggregate on trillion-param MoE" claim checks out: DeepSeek-R1-0528 FP8 on 8x L20 + dual Xeon Gold 6454S = 227.85 tok/s total / 87.58 tok/s output at 8-way concurrency (README + SGLang blog, 2025-10-22). Serving integration: SGLang became the serving path via the kvcache-ai fork sglang-kt (README feature line "Integrating into SGLang" dated 2025-10-10; lmsys.org blog 2025-10-22; sglang issue #11425); the blog's requirements are Intel AMX (Sapphire Rapids+) with AMXINT4 for int4 weights, CUDA >= 12.1, and ~500 GB+ DDR5 for DeepSeek-V3-sized experts; tested single-GPU rigs were A100 40GB or RTX 4080 16GB with dual-socket Xeon Platinum 8452Y (36c x2, 1TB DDR5 x2). vLLM was KT's selectable local attention backend in the early-2025 line but is absent from the current v0.7.0 README; the exact removal release is not pinned [uncertain]. Current packaging: kt-kernel PyPI wheel (CPU-optimized MoE kernels, "AMX, AVX, KML and blis", runtime auto-select among six CPU variants: AMX, AVX512+BF16, +VBMI, +VNNI, AVX512 base, AVX2) plus sglang-kt for production heterogeneous serving; wheel CPU baseline is AVX2 (Haswell 2013+/Zen+); an AVX2-only inference backend was added 2026-03-26, enabling leaderboard AVX2 rows from v0.5.3. Releases: v0.5.1/v0.5.3/v0.6.2.post3 (leaderboard versions), v0.6.1 (2026-04-30), v0.7.0 (2026-08-17, sglang-kt==0.7.0, LoRA fine-tuning on AVX512 CPUs without AMX, GLM-5.3-flash support 2026-08-26). Leaderboard (37 configs, fetched 2026-09-07) is entirely RTX 5090/4090/H20 GPUs with dual-socket server CPUs; no Turing/sm75 entry exists, ever. Key 35B-class rows: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B FP8 = 97.5 tok/s decode (4x RTX 5090, 2x EPYC 9355, v0.5.1), 93.2 (2x 5090), 86.2 (1x 5090), 60.9 (1x 5090, AVX2 CPU path, v0.5.3), 19.3 (1x RTX 4090 + 2x EPYC 7C13 AVX2, v0.5.3); Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16 = 19.4 tok/s (1x 4090 + 2x EPYC 7C13 AVX2) and 52.5 (1x 5090, AVX2). The 1x->2x GPU gain at 35B-A3B is only +8% (86.2->93.2): the lane is CPU-bound at this model size. Related systems: HybriMoE (arXiv:2504.05897) builds on KT; SGLang upstream generalizes the KT backend for multi-tier memory (sglang #11425).
sm75_viability: Hard floor: KTransformers cannot run on this host. The kt-kernel README (fetched 2026-09-07) requires "NVIDIA GPU with compute capability 8.0+ (Ampere or newer)"; its single wheel covers SM 80/86/89/90 only; the compatibility matrix explicitly marks Turing (cc 7.5, e.g., RTX 2080, T4) and Volta (V100, P100, GTX 1000/2000 series) as "not supported (too old)". Quadro RTX 6000 (TU102, cc 7.5) is below the floor at every release in KT history - there is no last-good sm75 base because sm75 was never supported. Reinforcing datapoint: even Ampere is second-class - issue #1978 (2026-05-04, A800 x4, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, closed) shows sm_80 lacks fp8e4nv ("seemingly unsolvable"; FP8 needs Ada/Hopper); community sm_75 adaptation writeups for DeepSeek-V4-Flash route through llama.cpp-style stacks, not KT. CPU side on this host: the W-2140B (Skylake-W, 8C/16T, quad-channel DDR4-2666 ~85 GB/s theoretical) has AVX512F+BW but no VNNI, no AVX512-BF16, no VBMI, no AMX, so kt-kernel would auto-select only the AVX512-base or AVX2 tier; the leaderboard's AVX2 floor was set by dual 64-core EPYC 7C13 rigs (roughly an order of magnitude more cores and ~4-5x the memory bandwidth of this host), and even those deliver just 19.3-19.4 tok/s decode at 35B-A3B with a 1x 4090 - an 8-core Skylake would land in single digits, if the GPU side could launch at all (it cannot). The only live CPU-resident-experts + GPU-attention topology on sm75 today is the llama.cpp family: --n-cpu-moe / -ncmoe / -ot ".ffn_.*_exps.=CPU". Measured precedent on the exact model class: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (35B total / 3B active, 40 layers, hybrid full+linear attention, 262K native context) Unsloth UD-IQ4_NL_XL (19.5 GiB) on a single RTX 3090 24 GB (gilesthomas.com, 2026-07-24, llama.cpp CUDA): 139.6 tok/s decode with 0 CPU-offloaded MoE layers (89.6K ctx), 89.1 tok/s with 10 layers offloaded (full 262K ctx), 84.9 at 12 layers; Vulkan build 51.4 tok/s at 20 layers (16.9 GB VRAM + 10.1 GB RAM). Scaling that to one RTX 6000 by the house-measured LDG bandwidth ratio (535 vs 936 GB/s) gives ~75-80 tok/s full-VRAM and ~48-51 tok/s partial-offload estimates [uncertain: derived, original CPU unspecified]. Attention-backend matrix for the sm75 analog: llama.cpp CUDA (works on sm75, ik_llama.cpp variant covered by the sibling-fork item) is the only path; SGLang itself is effectively Ampere+ (sglang #7467 per this run's records); KT is cc 8.0+. Fallback semantics: KT topology on this host = llama.cpp partial expert offload, whose only win over vLLM TP=2 is freeing VRAM for long-context KV - at 19.5-22.4 GiB the whole quant already fits one 24 GB card, and TP=2 gives 48 GB aggregate with all experts in VRAM. KT's own numbers confirm GPU TP adds little in this topology at this size (+8% for the second 5090), whereas vLLM TP=2 aggregates both cards' DRAM bandwidth for weight streaming.

effort_estimate: Three tiers. (a) Disposition (recommended): hours, zero code - record the cc-8.0+ citation and the lane pricing in the plan/0005 reconsideration; close the KT lane for this host. (b) Optional informational probe, ~1 day: pip install kt-kernel (AVX2-baseline wheel), run its standalone CPU MoE microbench via the Python API on the W-2140B at the AVX512-base tier, oracle-check outputs against a float64 reference per house discipline - prices what 8 Skylake cores would contribute to any hybrid topology; caveat: the wheel ships CUDA components targeting SM80+ and may fail import/init on a cc-7.5-only machine [uncertain]. (c) Making KT actually run here: not a software task of adapter-plus-registry-row size - it requires replacing the GPUs with Ampere+ cards and the CPU with an AMX (Sapphire Rapids/Granite Rapids or Xeon 6) or at minimum AVX512-VNNI-class multi-channel server part (the leaderboard rigs are all dual-socket, 8 memory channels per socket); that is a hardware campaign, not kernel work. (d) The sm75-live implementation of the same topology (llama.cpp/ik_llama.cpp -ncmoe on one RTX 6000 with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) is a benchmark session, and it belongs to the sibling-fork lane, not this item.
unlocks: On current hardware: nothing - blocked at the GPU compute-capability floor, and the operator's target Qwen3.8/Qwen3.8-Next (dense-GDN primary) are absent from KT's model registry and leaderboard. On the 35B-A3B-class secondary: the lane would only unlock capability the host does not already have if experts had to stay high-precision (BF16 ~66-70 GB exceeds 48 GB aggregate VRAM but fits 125 GB RAM) or for freeing VRAM as long-context KV via partial offload; at IQ4/W4A16 (19.5-22.4 GiB) the model is GPU-resident anyway, where vLLM TP=2 dominates. On suitable future hardware (Ampere+ GPU + AMX dual-socket): it would unlock >VRAM MoE serving (671B-class on a single 24 GB card at 10-20 tok/s, 227.85 tok/s aggregate on 8x L20).
dependency_order: No repo-internal dependencies: nothing in the kernel ladder, quant lanes, or engine items needs this, and this needs none of them - the item is fully parallel and terminates in a disposition. External prerequisites for any live use on this host: GPU cc >= 8.0 and an AMX/AVX512-VNNI-class multi-channel CPU, i.e., hardware that does not exist here; there is no order in which repo work makes KT runnable. If the operator wants the CPU-expert fallback semantic for the 35B secondary, the live path is the llama.cpp-family -ncmoe route, which rides the sibling-fork-ecosystem-crosspoll lane (ik_llama.cpp) and can proceed immediately in parallel.
risk_notes: KT's own numerics risks are moot on this host (unusable), but for the record: Expert Deferral is an accuracy-for-speed approximation (up to 1.45x throughput for <0.5% average accuracy change) - an approximation-style mechanism that violates this host's exact-execution-of-stored-values discipline; its prefill speedups depend on AMX-specialized kernels absent on Skylake. For the sm75 analog lane: GGUF IQ4/Q4_K quants are a different numeric contract from the house W4A16 AutoRound lane (different scale grids, im-quant mixes in IQ4_NL) - no oracle-parity claim carries over, and quality acceptance would have to be re-run rather than inherited; partial expert offload itself does not change numerics beyond the quant choice (no silent fallback in llama.cpp - layer placement is explicit via -ncmoe/-ot). Upstream-drift exposure: zero for KT (not consumed); for the llama.cpp analog, drift is owned by the sibling-fork item. The main correctness risk in any adoption decision is anchoring on KT's headline speedups (prefill up to 20x on dual-8452Y + 1TB DDR5 rigs) and assuming transfer to an 8-core Skylake - the leaderboard's own AVX2 rows (19.3 tok/s with a 4090 and 128 AVX2 cores) bound the disappointment in advance.
determinism_class: KTransformers: statistical, not bitwise - asynchronous CPU-GPU scheduling, CUDA-graph replay, batch-size-dependent hot/cold expert placement (deferred experts), and the Expert-Deferral approximation all make outputs batch- and load-dependent; incompatible with the float64-oracle + median-of-N gate discipline unless Deferral is disabled and single-stream decode is forced (and even then the stack is unrunnable here). llama.cpp analog (the only sm75-live version): single-stream CPU GEMM has no atomics; greedy or fixed-seed sampled decode is deterministic run-to-run and restart-to-restart; residual variance is thread-pool scheduling jitter in CPU-resident expert GEMMs (statistical, small, median-of-five handles it). The comparison lane, vLLM TP=2 GPU-resident, carries the atomics/split-K + NCCL-transport restart variance surface already owned by the tp2-decode-variance-engine item - meaning the determinism discipline favors GPU-resident TP=2 over any CPU-expert hybrid on this host, independent of speed.
priority_signal: Against doing this next (dominant): (1) hard hardware floor - kt-kernel requires cc 8.0+ and its matrix explicitly lists Turing as unsupported, so no amount of fork work revives it on 2x TU102; (2) the host CPU is an 8-core Skylake-W with AVX512-base only - roughly an order of magnitude below every rig on KT's leaderboard, whose weakest AVX2 floor (dual 64-core EPYC 7C13 + RTX 4090) already yields only ~19 tok/s at 35B-A3B; (3) operator focus is Qwen3.8 + Qwen3.8-Next (dense-GDN primary), which are not KT targets; (4) the 35B-A3B secondary at IQ4/W4A16 (19.5-22.4 GiB) fits one card, making CPU-resident experts a non-need on this host, and KT's own data shows a second GPU adds only +8% in its topology (CPU-bound) versus near-2x bandwidth aggregation under vLLM TP=2; (5) integration surface is empty - KT's serving path is sglang-kt, a fork of SGLang (itself Ampere-leaning), sharing zero code with this fork's vLLM engine and kernel investment, so adopting it would strand the sm75 execution-layer work. For keeping the lane documented: the CPU-expert idea remains the honest fallback semantic for any future >48 GB model, with the llama.cpp -ncmoe route as the only sm75-live implementation (RTX 3090 precedent: 89.1 tok/s at 10 layers offloaded, 51.4 at 20 layers, on the exact Qwen3.6-35B-A3B class); recording the infeasibility with citations prevents re-litigation at the plan/0005 reconsideration. Window-closing risk: none - the blocker is hardware, not a software window.
recommended_probe: Gate-0, oracle-first, no timing until numerics proven - and mostly a disposition probe because the main question is already answered by citation: (1) Zero-cost: record the kt-kernel cc-8.0+ compatibility-matrix citation plus the leaderboard CPU-class rows as the lane's closure evidence in the plan/0005 reconsideration; KT is closed for this host. (2) If the operator wants the 35B fallback priced (one session): llama.cpp CUDA build on one RTX 6000, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Unsloth UD-IQ4_NL_XL (19.5 GiB), -ngl all -fa on, sweep -ncmoe 0/10/12/20; first oracle-check logits at each -ncmoe setting against the same-build reference (fixed seed; confirms offload changes placement, not math), then median-of-five decode tok/s at locked clocks; accept the CPU-expert lane only if a partial-offload point beats the projected TP=2 W4A16 floor while freeing >=16 GB VRAM for KV - expectation from the 3090 precedent scaled by 535/936 GB/s says it will not. (3) Optional 1-day informational probe of the CPU question with data: kt-kernel standalone Python API on the W-2140B, CPU MoE microbench at the AVX512-base tier, float64 oracle on the kernel outputs; if (unexpectedly) 8 Skylake cores deliver more than single-digit effective tok/s at 35B-A3B active weights, reopen the item - otherwise the CPU prerequisite line (AMX / AVX512-VNNI dual-socket, 8 channels per socket) stands as written [uncertain: whether kt-kernel imports cleanly without a cc>=8.0 GPU present].
